name: Joshua Reynolds
findings: Uses smoky black 2.5x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 670 paintings here).
Uses dark walnut 1.7x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 670 paintings here).
Uses dark olive brown 1.5x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 670 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, sand turns up as a small accent in 45% of the paintings that hold it, 3.2x the archive's rate (from 670 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, mole brown turns up as the lightest note in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 4.0x the archive's rate (from 670 paintings here).
Pairs liver brown with umber more than chance would predict (3 of 670 paintings here).
Pairs beige grey with bone brown more than chance would predict (3 of 670 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, raisin black, black) covers 57% of his paintings here.
